description.narrative:
The overarching goal of Diakonias country strategy for Colombia is to mobilise society for peacebuilding, making the conditions for peace a national priority. In particular, the organisation identifies the holistic implementation of existing peace accords, strengthened guarantees for the protection and safety of civil society organisations and the initiation of new peace-talks, as such prioritised conditions for peace.
To achieve this, Diakonia proposes to strengthen and to work together with local civil society organisations to generate significant changes and structural transformations in four interrelated areas or change processes, each with its own set of objectives and results indicators:
1. Strengthened capacity of civil society to exercise democratic participation, defence of human rights and active citizenship. 2. Implementation of the peace agreements, new peace-talks and national reconciliation. 3. Increased gender equality in social, economic and political structures. 4. Environmental justice and defence of the right to a healthy environment

Kärnstödet till Diakonia i Colombia syftar till att bidra till en stabil och varaktig fred i landet med ett nationellt, territoriellt och rättighetsbaserat perspektiv. Detta stöd är en fortsättning av en tidigare insats med ID 10781. De övergripande målen är följande:
1) Stärkt kapacitet hos det civila samhället att utöva demokratiskt deltagande, försvar av mänskliga rättigheter och aktivt medborgarskap. 2) Genomförande av fredsavtalet, nya fredssamtal och nationell försoning. 3) Ökad jämställdhet i sociala, ekonomiska och politiska strukturer. 4) Miljörättvisa och försvar av rätten till en hälsosam miljö.

The support to Diakonia cointains two components; a core funding to the country plan; and a project support to a civil society fund. The components aim at contributing to a stable and lasting peace in Colombia with a national, territorial, and right-based perspective. The overall objectives are the following:
1) Strengthened capacity of civil society to exercise democratic participation, defence of human rights and active citizenship. 2) Implementation of the peace agreement, new peace-talks, and national reconciliation. 3) Increased gender equality in social, economic, and political structures. 4) Environmental justice and defence of the right to a healthy environment.
This support is a continuation of previous contribution with ID-number 10781.

description.narrative:
The following section will mostly focus on results achieved during 2023, with some exception (UM2021/15109/BOGO78). For more information on results achieved during 2022, see the narrative report (UM2021/15109/BOGO57).
Diakonia in Colombia achieved results in peacebuilding, human rights protection, gender inclusion, and environmental defense. Expected outcomes included the establishment of humanitarian agreements and the strengthening of protection mechanisms for human rights defenders, which played a crucial role in ensuring their safety in a context of ongoing risks.
The work of diakonia through its partners have helped to the establishment of humanitarian agreements and regional humanitarian tables, aimed at containing conflict and paving the way for peace negotiations. This approach has fostered a deep connection between peace construction, human rights perspectives, and humanitarian action focused on International Humanitarian Law (IHL).
Ethnic and territorial partners, including Indigenous peoples and AfroColombian communities, have shifted their attitudes towards gender equality by developing internal gender policies. This change has led to women occupying decisionmaking positions and an increased interest in elevating women's leadership and rights, marking a departure from previous views that considered gender agendas divisive.
The target groups, particularly local organizations and communities, have improved designing protection plans, managing funds for selfprotection, and engaging in advocacy for effective state responses to ensure the safety of human rights defenders. This newfound capability enhances their resilience against risks and aggressions associated with defending their territories and rights. . By strengthening the protection of human rights defenders, empowering women and feminist partners, and facilitating the development of internal gender policies within ethnic organizations, Diakonia has contributed to a safer, more inclusive, and equitable environment for advocating peace, human rights, and environmental protection in Colombia.
Civil Society Fund component have facilitated a collaborative environment among Swedish NGO and thematic advisors, leading to established work agreements and team functionality. This has prepared the team for a more agile start to projects in 2024. The fund has managed to deliver 13 grants across various regions, demonstrating a broad presence and thematic diversity. Organizations that received financing appreciated the financial and political support, marking a change in their capacity to carry out peacebuilding, human rights, and protection of defenders' work. For some, it was their first experience receiving funds from an international NGO, indicating a new level of operational capability. There has been a concerted effort to improve coordination and dialogue with organizations from the proposal submission phase, suggesting a shift towards more transparent and communicative relationships. In summary, the Civil Society Fund's operations have made an important impact through financial and political support to partner organizations, emphasizing a territorial approach and institutional strengthening.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
